title_en: Announcement of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Ministry of Justice on the Implementation Measures for the National Judicial Examination (Trial)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Justice

Announcement on the "Implementation Measures for the National Judicial Examination (Interim)"

No. 2

Pursuant to the provisions of the amendments to the Judges Law of the People's Republic of China and the Procurators Law of the People's Republic of China, the Ministry of Justice, in conjunction with the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate, has formulated the "Implementation Measures for the National Judicial Examination (Interim)", which are hereby promulgated.

These Measures shall come into force as of January 1, 2002.

Implementation Measures for the National Judicial Examination (Interim)

Chapter I: General Provisions

Article 1 These Measures are formulated in accordance with the Judges Law of the People's Republic of China, the Procurators Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Lawyers Law of the People's Republic of China for the purpose of establishing and standardizing the system of a uniform national judicial examination, and improving and guaranteeing the quality of the ranks of judges, procurators, and lawyers.

Article 2 The National Judicial Examination is a qualification examination uniformly organized by the state for engaging in specific legal professions.

Those who are to be initially appointed as judges or initial procurators, and those who are to obtain lawyer qualification, must pass the National Judicial Examination.

Article 3 The National Judicial Examination shall be fair and equitable.

Article 4 The Ministry of Justice, in conjunction with the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate, shall form the National Judicial Examination Coordination Committee to consult on major matters concerning the National Judicial Examination.

Article 5 The National Judicial Examination shall be implemented by the Ministry of Justice.

Chapter II: The Examination

Article 6 The National Judicial Examination shall be held once a year. The specific examination date shall be announced to the public three months before the examination.

Article 7 The National Judicial Examination mainly tests the legal professional knowledge that candidates should possess and their ability to engage in the legal profession.

The content of the National Judicial Examination includes: theoretical jurisprudence, applied jurisprudence, current legal provisions, legal practice, and legal professional ethics.

Article 8 The National Judicial Examination shall adopt a nationally unified question-setting system.

The scope of questions for the National Judicial Examination shall be based on the "National Judicial Examination Outline" formulated and published by the Ministry of Justice.

Article 9 The National Judicial Examination shall be conducted in a closed-book format.

Article 10 The National Judicial Examination shall adopt a nationally unified grading system, and the results shall be announced by the Ministry of Justice.

Chapter III: Examination Organization

Article 11 The Ministry of Justice shall establish a specialized body to specifically undertake the work of the National Judicial Examination.

Matters concerning examination administration, including registration, examination venue setup, examination discipline, invigilation, and grading, shall be separately prescribed by the Ministry of Justice in accordance with these Measures.

Article 12 The departments of justice (bureaus) of each province, autonomous region, and municipality directly under the Central Government shall establish specialized bodies to be specifically responsible for the detailed examination administration work within their respective jurisdictions.

Chapter IV: Registration Conditions

Article 13 Persons who meet the following conditions may register to take the National Judicial Examination:

(1) Possessing the nationality of the People's Republic of China;

(2) Upholding the Constitution of the People's Republic of China and enjoying the right to vote and the right to be elected;

(3) Possessing full capacity for civil conduct;

(4) Meeting the educational background and professional conditions prescribed by the Judges Law, the Procurators Law, and the Lawyers Law;

(5) Having good conduct.

Article 14 Persons who fall under any of the following circumstances may not register to take the examination; if registration formalities have already been completed, the registration shall be invalid:

(1) Having been subjected to criminal punishment for an intentional crime;

(2) Having been dismissed from public office by a state organ, or having had their lawyer's practicing certificate revoked;

(3) Having been subjected to a sanction of being prohibited from registering to take the National Judicial Examination for two years or permanently, in accordance with the provisions of Article 18 of these Measures.

Chapter V: Granting of Qualifications

Article 15 The passing number for each annual examination and the qualifying score line for the National Judicial Examination shall be announced by the Ministry of Justice after consultation with the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate.

Article 16 Persons who pass the National Judicial Examination shall be issued a "Legal Professional Qualification Certificate" by the Ministry of Justice.

Article 17 If a "Legal Professional Qualification Certificate" is obtained in violation of the provisions of these Measures, it shall be deemed invalid by the Ministry of Justice.

Chapter VI: Responsibilities

Article 18 If candidates commit acts of cheating or other disciplinary violations, they shall, depending on the circumstances and consequences, be subject to sanctions including warnings, a declaration that the examination results are invalid, and prohibition from registering to take the National Judicial Examination for two years or permanently. Specific measures for handling such matters shall be prescribed by the Ministry of Justice.

Article 19 If examination staff commit disciplinary violations, they shall be subject to corresponding sanctions depending on the circumstances and consequences; if the circumstances are particularly serious and constitute a crime, they shall be dealt with by the judicial authorities. Specific measures shall be prescribed by the Ministry of Justice.

Chapter VII: Supplementary Provisions

Article 20 If necessary, examination papers in ethnic minority languages and scripts may be used in minority nationality regions.

Article 21 The amendment and interpretation of these Measures shall be carried out by the Ministry of Justice after consultation with the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and shall be published by the Ministry of Justice.

Article 22 These Measures shall come into force as of January 1, 2002.
